events.title: Heraclius reaches Constantinople to overthrow Phocas
events.description: Heraclius, son of the exarch of Africa, arrived at Constantinople with a fleet from Carthage and toppled the unpopular emperor Phocas. His reign saw triumph over Persia but also the loss of Syria and Egypt to the Arabs.

events.title: Catholic Europe switches to the Gregorian calendar
events.description: In Italy, Spain, Portugal and Poland, Thursday 4 October 1582 was followed directly by Friday 15 October. Pope Gregory XIII's reform dropped ten days to realign the calendar with the solar year.
events.html: In Italy, Spain, Portugal and Poland, Thursday 4 October 1582 was followed directly by Friday 15 October. Pope Gregory XIII's reform dropped ten days to realign the calendar with the solar year.

events.title: Belgium's provisional government declares independence
events.description: Following the September uprising in Brussels, Belgium's provisional government declared independence from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. The great powers recognised the new state, and later guaranteed its neutrality.

events.title: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1
events.description: The Soviet Union placed Sputnik 1, an 84-kilogram metal sphere, into orbit, the first artificial satellite. Its radio beeps, picked up worldwide, shocked the West and launched the Space Race.

events.title: Paul VI becomes the first pope to visit the United States
events.description: Pope Paul VI flew to New York for a one-day visit, the first by a reigning pope to the United States. He appealed for peace at the United Nations General Assembly and celebrated Mass at Yankee Stadium.
